directions.description: Add renaming/relabeling equivariance (invariance of the per-coordinate machinery under permuting which coordinate is assigned which formal nilpotent symbol, given isomorphic per-coordinate Weil algebras) as an explicit hypothesis on the construction, and test Melchior's two concrete candidate cross-term gluing maps against it on the same-order case W_1=W_2=R[e]/(e^2).
directions.routes_around: Melchior's located gap (two natural, inequivalent candidate projections for cross-coordinate nilpotent terms, no adjudication supplied) — proposes the missing adjudication principle as a hypothesis placed exactly at the located obstruction.
directions.heuristic: [HEURISTIC] A naming-symmetry requirement is the kind of constraint that plausibly discriminates between an index-blind 'kill mixed terms' projection and a total-degree truncation that may not be index-blind; untested.

directions.description: Rather than testing candidates against relabeling-equivariance, construct the cross-term gluing map directly via symmetrization/coinvariants (averaging-operator style) under the relabeling group action, so the map is equivariant by construction for general coupled vector fields.
directions.routes_around: Same Melchior gap, but manufactures the missing compatibility structure via an invariant-theoretic averaging construction instead of enumerating and checking ad hoc guesses, and instead of importing the KMS base/fiber functor's different (non-symmetrization) compatibility shape.
directions.heuristic: [HEURISTIC] Symmetrization/averaging over a relabeling group is a standard way invariant theory manufactures canonical maps from non-canonical raw data; whether the resulting map is nonzero, well-typed, or coincides with an already-found candidate is unconfirmed.
